findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted (it rejects the token when the grant shortcut matches) and also uses the wrong offsets: the encoded 6-char prefix is sessionType (chars 0-2), tokenType (chars 2-4), grantType (chars 4-6), so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. As written the matcher fails for valid tokens with the expected grant and passes for tokens with the wrong grant, so none of the TOKEN_ID assertions in expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken actually verify the new encoding.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` a second time instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted, which will later produce an encoded token ID like "onrtac:null" (or an NPE during string concatenation in encodeTokenId), corrupting the token ID.

findings.title: getShortcut() added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation
findings.body: Adding the abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks binary/source compatibility for any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations (custom grant type extensions): they will fail to load with AbstractMethodError at runtime or fail to compile. A `default` implementation (e.g. returning getId()) would preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) removed
findings.body: The PR deletes the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor from the SPI class OAuth2GrantType.Context. Any external code (custom grant types or extensions) relying on that constructor will break at compile time or with NoSuchMethodError at runtime. Note also that the new main constructor now captures grantType from formParams, so setFormParams() after construction leaves a stale grantType — a behavior change for anyone using setFormParams.

findings.title: Decoder assumes exactly 6-char context prefix but encoder accepts arbitrary-length grant shortcuts
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars, while encodeTokenId happily concatenates whatever getShortcut() returns (the SPI javadoc even says "usually like 3-letters shortcut"). A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a shortcut of length != 2 will produce token IDs that this provider itself cannot decode — any endpoint later calling getTokenContextFromTokenId on such a token will throw IllegalArgumentException. The factory should validate shortcut length (and charset) at startup, or the decoder should be tolerant.

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws on malformed legacy/foreign token IDs instead of degrading to UNKNOWN
findings.body: Token IDs without ':' are gracefully mapped to UNKNOWN context, but an ID containing ':' with a prefix that is 6 chars yet uses an unknown session/token/grant shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException. Since token IDs are attacker-influenced input at endpoints like introspection, any future caller of this method must be prepared for exceptions; returning UNKNOWN context (as done for legacy IDs) would be a safer, consistent contract. Also note OAuth2GrantType IDs like the pre-authorized-code URN contain ':' — if a grant ID were ever used as an ID component this parsing would misbehave, so the contract 'throws on anything not self-encoded' should be documented on the SPI interface.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut detection via map size comparison is fragile
findings.body: The duplicate detection only compares map sizes; it detects a shared shortcut only indirectly and its error message is confusing. It also does not detect the case where a grant uses the reserved shortcut "na" (which would silently overwrite the UNKNOWN mapping in both maps, keeping sizes equal and passing validation), after which tokens with unknown grant type would decode as that grant type. An explicit duplicate check while populating would be correct and give a clear error.

findings.title: userSession may be null when deriving session type
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext calls clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and immediately dereferences it. For client-credentials grants the client session may not be attached to a user session in all paths (UserSessionModel can be null in some service-account implementations); if any caller invokes this with a detached client session, an NPE is thrown during token creation. The code should null-check and fall back to UNKNOWN/transient.
